clue.text: Sound move, plain to Nikita

indicators.note: a sound version of the next word is one heard rather than seen, so it is spoken and respelt

blocks.note: a move made by the foot, said out loud

explanation.surface: A Russian leader is told how to cross his flat grasslands.
explanation.walkthrough: Nikita is Khrushchev, so the plain is a Russian one: the steppe, which is pronounced just like step.
explanation.definitionFit: The steppe is the vast treeless grassland of Russia and Central Asia, the plain a Russian such as Khrushchev would know.

clue.text: Loses footing, to fall on board

indicators.note: being on board means being inside a ship, so the fall goes inside the steamship letters

blocks.note: a tumble is a fall
SS, steamship, is the usual crossword ship for anything on board

explanation.surface: A passenger slips and goes down on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' does double duty, signalling the putting inside and naming the ship; SS for steamship is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stumbles trips and briefly loses balance, which is exactly losing one's footing.

clue.text: There are two points he can possibly raise

indicators.note: possibly suggests just one of many arrangements, so the letters of he can are rearranged

blocks.note: two compass points, east and north
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man spots two scoring chances in a game and wonders if he can push up the total.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to improve or heighten it, a synonym of raising its level or value.

clue.text: It's the limit, figuratively speaking

blocks.note: surface reading: an exasperated cry that something is beyond bearing
setter's reading: speaking of geometric figures, the boundary line round a shape

explanation.walkthrough: 'Figuratively speaking' usually means metaphorically; here it means in the language of figures, as in geometry, where the outer edge is the limit.
explanation.definitionFit: A perimeter is the boundary or outer edge of a shape or area, its limit in a literal sense.

clue.text: Bones of poet found outside European capital

indicators.note: a capital is the head letter of a word, so only its opening letter is kept
the poet is found outside, wrapped around the other letter

blocks.note: John Skelton, Tudor poet
the head of the word European

explanation.surface: A writer's remains are discovered just beyond a city such as Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European capital' looks like a city to name, but it is only the capital letter of European. Skelton was poet laureate under Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the full framework of bones in a body, so the bones collectively are the skeleton.

clue.text: Tolstoy's novel musical work takes a turn with zero complications

indicators.note: complications tangle things up, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
more letters for the mix

explanation.surface: A piece of music lurches unexpectedly through some tangled episodes.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions sit at the front: the Beethoven violin sonata, and the Tolstoy novella named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Kreutzer Sonata is a famous violin work, and Tolstoy borrowed its name for his 1889 novella about jealousy.

clue.text: Composer many hear when wandering

indicators.note: wandering means roaming off course, so the letters of hear stray into a new order

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, a crossword many
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer's tunes reach plenty of listeners as they stroll about.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Lehár wrote the operetta The Merry Widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was the Hungarian-born writer of operettas such as The Merry Widow, so a classic composer.

clue.text: Hints about a vessel for vegetables

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hints wrap round the vessel

blocks.note: tips are hints
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Cooking advice on which pot to use for boiling your greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnips are root crops eaten as vegetables, an example of the class named.

clue.text: Turn on at length an item on the programme

blocks.note: first meaning: a turn, a performer's act, here one that goes on at length
second meaning: a piece listed in a concert or show

explanation.walkthrough: A turn is a music-hall act; 'on at length' only colours it as an act that runs long. Both senses are the same word for a performance piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a single act, song or routine in a show, the same thing as a variety turn or programme item.

clue.text: Those he led _ may have been legion

definitions.text: Those he led _ may have been legion

blocks.note: surface reading: legion as an adjective, meaning there were very many followers
setter's reading: he marched in front carrying the eagle of a Roman legion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Legion' looks like 'countless', as in 'their name is legion'; it is a Roman army unit. The underscore is a mark from the scan.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard-bearer carries a unit's flag or eagle, and in Rome that unit was a legion following behind.

clue.text: Torch-bearer being a Girl Guide

blocks.note: surface reading: a member of the youth movement, perhaps carrying a torch
setter's reading: a girl who guides cinemagoers to their seats with a flashlight

explanation.walkthrough: The Girl Guides are the British Girl Scouts, but here it is just a girl who guides, the woman in an old cinema who showed patrons to seats by torchlight.
explanation.definitionFit: An usherette was a female cinema attendant who led audiences to their seats using a hand torch.

clue.text: Where in the house sultanas are found

definitions.text: Where in the house sultanas are found

blocks.note: surface reading: dried grapes, kept in a kitchen cupboard
setter's reading: the quarters of a sultan's household where his wives live

explanation.walkthrough: Sultanas are raisins, but a sultana is also a sultan's wife, and the wives lived in their own part of the palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The harem is the secluded women's section of a Muslim household, where a sultan's wives and concubines lived.

clue.text: Fleming in servitude ?

blocks.note: setter's reading: Ian Fleming's man is his hero, Bond
plain reading: a serf or slave bound to a master

explanation.walkthrough: Ian Fleming's man is James Bond, so a Bond man; read as one word it is an old term for a serf.
explanation.definitionFit: A bondman was a feudal serf or slave, a person held in servitude to a master.

clue.text: In its turn it does us a power of good

definitions.text: In its turn it does us a power of good

blocks.clueFragment: does us a power of good
blocks.note: surface reading: an idiom for something very beneficial, like a tonic
setter's reading: a machine whose rotating blades generate power for us

explanation.walkthrough: 'A power of good' is an idiom for great benefit, and 'in its turn' sounds like 'for its part'; both are literal here, about spinning and electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbine is a rotary engine driven by water, steam or wind, used to generate electrical power.

clue.text: Even he leaves the special occasion

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so those two letters go out of the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before losing letters

explanation.surface: Even this fellow walks out of the big celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is not a person but two letters removed from 'the', leaving T to follow EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a notable happening or planned function, such as a special occasion.

clue.text: Twelfth foundation stone, St John revealed

definitions.text: Twelfth foundation stone, St John revealed

blocks.note: surface reading: the last stone laid at the base of a building
setter's reading: the Book of Revelation, ascribed to John, lists the jewels of the New Jerusalem's walls

explanation.walkthrough: In Revelation 21 the wall of the heavenly city has twelve foundations, each a gem; the twelfth is the violet one.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelation 21:20 names the purple quartz gem as the twelfth precious stone garnishing the city's foundations.

clue.text: Farm servant hurried to church. Despite this obstacle?

blocks.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer
ran means hurried
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A farmhand dashes to the service, getting there in spite of some impediment.
explanation.walkthrough: A hind was a farm worker in older English and Scots; CE, the Church of England, is the usual crossword church.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is something that impedes progress, a straightforward synonym of an obstacle.

clue.text: Incautious but avoiding ruin, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the phrase before it is said out loud and respelt

blocks.note: free of wrecks, as if never ruined

explanation.surface: A careless driver somehow escapes disaster, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reckless means acting without heed to danger, which is a synonym for being incautious.

clue.text: Gate-crashes and has a bad turn inside, perhaps

definitions.text: has a bad turn inside, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: arrives uninvited

blocks.clueFragment: has a bad turn inside, perhaps
blocks.note: second meaning, playing on the word itself: its middle letters are a jumbled turn

explanation.walkthrough: The second half describes the word: I(NTRU)DES holds a bad, mixed-up TURN inside, with IDES around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To gate-crash is to enter where one is not invited, which is to intrude on others' privacy.

clue.text: It's accidentally raised in sharp practice

definitions.text: It's accidentally raised in sharp practice

blocks.note: surface reading: dishonest dealing, crookedness
setter's reading: in music practice an accidental sign that cancels a flat, putting the note back up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp practice' is cheating, but the clue means musical practice with sharps; this accidental sign raises a flattened note back to normal pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: In notation a natural is an accidental that cancels a flat or sharp, restoring the unaltered pitch of a note.

clue.text: Ingenuous Welsh lad returns to embrace one

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the lad's name runs backwards
embracing means holding inside the arms, so the name wraps round the one

blocks.note: Evan is a typical Welsh boy's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An innocent young Welshman comes home and hugs someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Evan, the Welsh form of John, is a stock crossword Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive and ingenuous both describe someone innocent and unsuspecting, lacking worldly guile; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Little caprices of life which gave Hardy his title 171. Sarah's crazy to worry

definitions.text: Little caprices of life which gave Hardy his title

blocks.note: surface reading: the small whims of fortune
setter's reading: Thomas Hardy's story collection Life's Little ... names these twists
surface padding: the next clue's text run on by the scan, not part of this clue

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy's 1894 story collection is Life's Little Ironies. The trailing '171. Sarah's crazy to worry' is the next clue run on by the scan.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironies are twists of fate where outcomes mock expectations, the perverse caprices that Hardy's stories trace.

clue.text: Sarah's crazy to worry

indicators.note: something crazy is all over the place, so the letters of the name are jumbled

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: A woman is frantic enough to fret about everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass is to pester and torment persistently, the same as to worry someone in the sense of bothering them.

clue.text: Its rate is adjusted for an entertainer

indicators.note: adjusted means changed about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Artiste is a theatrical word for a professional performer such as a singer or dancer, so an entertainer.

clue.text: Divide the rent

blocks.note: first meaning: to separate into parts
second meaning: a rent is a tear or crack

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about housemates sharing housing costs, but rent here is a tear, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for separating into parts and a noun for a tear or crack in something.

clue.text: Where we see dumplings in their jackets?

definitions.text: Where we see dumplings in their jackets?

blocks.note: surface reading: food cooked in its skin, like jacket potatoes
setter's reading: an English county known for its dumplings and for a belted tweed jacket

explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk is an English county famous for Norfolk dumplings and the belted Norfolk jacket; 'dumplings' also hints at plump locals.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Anglian county gives its name both to a style of dumpling and to a belted country jacket.

clue.text: Its foolish start is shortlived

blocks.note: setter's reading: the month that opens with Fools' Day
surface reading: a silly beginning soon fades; truly, a month of only thirty days

explanation.walkthrough: The first day of this month is Fools' Day, for pranks until noon, and the month itself is one of the shorter ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month opens with All Fools' Day and has just thirty days, a short span.

clue.text: Traditionally . descriptive of Kala Nags' memory

definitions.text: Traditionally . descriptive of Kala Nags' memory

blocks.note: setter's reading: Kala Nag is Kipling's elephant, and elephants never forget
surface reading: an old-fashioned way to describe something

explanation.walkthrough: Kala Nag is the elephant in Kipling's story Toomai of the Elephants; by tradition an elephant never forgets. The stray full stop is a scan mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A retentive memory holds on to what it learns, which is the proverbial quality of an elephant's recall.

clue.text: Like Wordsworth's reaper — describing confinement in prison

blocks.note: first meaning: his poem The ... Reaper, about a lone Highland girl
second meaning: the kind of confinement where a prisoner is kept alone

explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's poem is The Solitary Reaper; solitary confinement is a prisoner isolated from others.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means alone or isolated, fitting both the lone girl in the poem and an isolated prisoner's cell.

clue.text: .popular form of enumeration?

blocks.note: surface reading: well liked; setter's reading: of the populace, the people
setter's reading: a counting, as of every person in a country

explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular' looks like 'well liked' but means 'of the population'. The leading full stop is a scan mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of a country's population, a counting of the people rather than a favoured method.
